Before you hire a TikTok Shop agency, ask questions that force specifics, because vague answers hide resellers. The single most revealing one is whether they will tie any fee to the GMV they drive. Below are 15 questions, grouped, that tell you fast whether you are talking to an operator or a middleman.

On accountability

  1. Will you tie part of your fee to the GMV you drive? The best filter. Operators say yes in some form.
  2. What GMV outcome would you commit to, and by when?
  3. What happens if we do not hit it?

On specialization

  1. Is TikTok Shop your focus, or one of many services? Specialists beat generalists here.
  2. What categories and price points have you actually sold? Vague answers are a flag.
  3. What have you learned in my category specifically?

On process

  1. How do you find and vet creators? Listen for selling behavior, not follower count.
  2. Walk me through your seeding process. Curated list, tracking, follow-up.
  3. How do you set commissions? By margin and product, not one blanket rate.
  4. How do you brief creators? Direction without over-scripting. Ask to see a brief.
  5. How do you handle ads? Amplifying proven content, not boosting randomly.

On reporting and operations

  1. What does your reporting show? GMV, GMV per creator, organic vs ad split, not "messages sent."
  2. Who runs my account day to day? Beware sold-by-a-closer, delivered-by-an-intern.

On the deal

  1. What is the contract length and how do I exit? Watch for long lock-ins before proof.
  2. Can you show one real account result, honestly stated? Not a platform-wide GMV brag; remember GMV is not revenue.

The tell behind the answers

Beyond the specific questions, listen for whether they can teach, not just pitch. An operator who ran a TikTok Shop agency noted that publishing real "case studies, how-tos, playbooks" gave him "100s of inbound leads" that were "pre-sold, almost 70% close rate" because the work "built authority" (@brian_blum1 on X). Ask an agency to walk you through a real playbook. The ones who have run programs can; the resellers deflect.

How to read the answers

  • Specifics and a willingness to share risk signal an operator.
  • Deflection on accountability, vague proof, and "messages sent" reporting signal a reseller.
  • Generalist positioning ("we do all social") usually means an Instagram playbook applied to a channel that does not work that way.

Print this list and run it on every agency you talk to, including us. For the full framework, see how to choose a TikTok Shop agency.

The takeaway

The right questions make quality obvious in ten minutes. Push for specifics on accountability, process, and reporting, and the resellers reveal themselves.
